lines: The painting had not been stolen.
That was the part the museum could not forgive.
Nobody had cut it from its frame, or smashed a case, or cut a wire.
At closing time the Dutch landscape was on the third-floor wall.
At opening time a different Dutch landscape was, and no one had told the paint.
It took the night guard, an old man named Folarin who had counted the same wall for twenty years, to notice the sky.
The forger had been brilliant: the brushwork, the varnish, the cracks.

What he had not understood, because he had never stood in front of it at four in the morning, as Folarin had, was that the original had a small, private weather, a storm that was always about to break and never did.
The copy had only ever been told what the sky looked like.
The old man knew what it felt like.
